_comment: Economic parameters: harvest yields, spoilage, price curves, upkeep rates. Filled in during Phase 1.
_harvestNote: Weather is drawn from named BANDS rather than a narrow bell curve, so years are memorable: a drought is a disaster you talk about, not a 15% dip. Weighted mean is ~1.02, so the long run is near-neutral while any single year can ruin or make a reign. withinBandJitter adds texture inside a band without blurring the bands into each other.
_storageNote: Grain keeps a couple of seasons, not forever: at 18% a year roughly half survives three years, so a reserve is a real but wasting asset. Was 30%, which combined with a thin surplus put the EQUILIBRIUM reserve at only ~1.3 years — below what a drought (0.3x harvest) requires — so realms could not build a survivable buffer however well they were played, and population declined to extinction over two centuries. The capacity ceiling (in years of consumption) is what actually stops hoarding; spoilage only needs to make grain perishable, not worthless.
_upkeepNote: Per-building upkeep now lives in data/buildings.json alongside each building's other specs. This section only holds cross-cutting upkeep that isn't tied to a single building type.
_consumptionNote: populationGrainRequirement was 0.5 against a per-peasant yield of 12.5 (5 ha at 2.5) — a 25x surplus, which is not an agricultural economy at all. It made grain worthless, stockpiles meaningless, sabotage loot pointless and weather irrelevant. At 9.0 a peasant produces roughly 1.4x what they eat: an ordinary year leaves a real but modest surplus, a lean year eats into the reserve, and a drought is a genuine famine.
_espionageNote: Guards and saboteurs are STANDING forces with annual upkeep, not one-off purchases. That makes a secret service a recurring burden rather than a bought-once advantage, and gives the late game another cost that scales with ambition.
_sabotageNote: Sabotage carries off grain AND a modest share of the treasury, per the original (docs/kaiser-research.md: burns buildings and transfers grain/currency to the attacker). A dedicated raid still takes far more coin; sabotage trades some of that for destroying a workshop outright.
_grainMarketNote: The Kaiser buys surplus corn and sells it back dearer. The spread is what makes storing versus selling a real decision rather than an arithmetic one, and it gives the early game an income source before any market or mill exists.
_populationRatesNote: Rates were 2%/1% for a net +1%/yr, which could not recover from the event pressure Phase 6 deliberately created: measured over 200 years, natural increase plus immigration came to +2,779 while plague and revolt took -2,947, so realms shrank to extinction no matter how well they were played. A pre-modern population facing mortality that heavy needs a correspondingly high birth rate — this is how real medieval populations rebuilt after plague years. Deaths rose too, so the gross churn is high and the NET is a modest +2.1%/yr: recovery is possible but slow enough that a bad decade still hurts for a generation.
